analysis.investment_thesis: Bikaji trades at 66x earnings and 11x book value — my Graham Number is approximately ₹102 against a market price of ₹660, a 6.5x premium to intrinsic value — making this among the most speculative valuations I have encountered. The snack business has real growth (revenue CAGR 19.5%), but I categorically refuse to pay 11x book for a packaged foods company regardless of its growth narrative.
key_strengths: Consistent profitability across all 5 years with net profit CAGR of 28.2% — earnings continuity is present
5/5 years of positive operating cash flow with Debt/Equity of 0.19 — balance sheet is sound
Interest coverage ratio of ~22x (EBITDA ₹356 Cr / finance cost ₹16 Cr) — minimal leverage risk
key_risks: P/E of 66.3 and P/B of 11.05 leave no margin of safety whatsoever under any conservative valuation
Net profit in FY2025 (₹194 Cr) fell from FY2024 (₹263 Cr) despite revenue growth — margin compression is real
Operating margin of only 9.4% in a commodity-input business makes earnings vulnerable to input cost inflation
red_flags: P/B of 11.05 — I regard anything above 2.0 as paying an excessive premium over assets; 11x is egregious
Net profit declined year-over-year in FY2025 while P/E expanded — investors are paying more for less
Borrowings tripled from ₹87 Cr (FY2021) to ₹310 Cr (FY2025) while capex is accelerating — capex cycle risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Graham Number: with EPS ~₹7.73 and BVPS ~₹59.8, the upper bound of fair value is ₹102. At ₹660, the market is pricing in years of flawless high-growth execution with no room for disappointment. This is precisely the kind of 'story stock' I warned against in The Intelligent Investor — the brand may be excellent, but the price demands perfection.

The FY2025 results are actually concerning upon inspection: while revenue grew 13% to ₹2,622 Cr, net profit contracted from ₹263 Cr to ₹194 Cr, implying margin deterioration. Operating income also fell from ₹392 Cr to ₹330 Cr year-over-year. A growth stock that shows margin compression at this valuation is doubly dangerous — the market will eventually reprice it harshly. No dividend yield of consequence further underscores the speculative character of this investment.
